prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a high-angle workspace where the camera wearer stands above and behind a seated person in a grey hoodie on the left (about 0.6 to 0.9 metres away) while a desk with a monitor, reel-to-reel tape machine, and mounted screen sits in front of both at roughly 0.8 to 1.3 metres. In frames 1 and 2, the wearer's both hands hold a smartphone on a small tripod very close to the chest (0.2 to 0.4 metres, brightest foreground), and across frames 3 to 5 the wearer extends their right arm forward (to about 0.6 to 0.8 metres) to place the phone on the desk between the seated person's mounted screen (approx. 0.4 metres from the seated person) and the computer monitor to its right. The seated person faces forward toward the desk and away from the camera wearer throughout, with their lower body occluded by the chair and frame edge, while the wearer's extended arm partially occludes the desk keyboard and mouse in the later frames. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the foreground elevation of the wearer's hands, the mid-ground seated person and paper-backed screen, and the receding wall and shelf on the upper left. However, the depth map is unreliable around thin tripod legs that merge into the background, and it assigns overly dark (distant) values to the dark casing of the reel-to-reel player and the gap behind the desk despite their similar true distance to the monitor.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map identifies up to three object classes—'person', 'tv' (the computer monitor on the right), and 'potted plant' (a small plant on the desk in frames 4 and 5)—establishing the monitor at roughly 1.0 to 1.2 metres in the upper right and people in the foreground and left mid-ground (0.2 to 0.9 metres). Across the sequence, the map tracks the camera wearer's shifting reach as their hands move from the bottom centre (frames 1–2, 0.2–0.4 metres) to the right-centre foreground (frames 3–5, extending to ~0.7 metres) while the seated person remains below and to the left, facing away toward the desk within arm's reach of the mounted screen and keyboard. While the mask shapes help isolate the planar boundary of the monitor and the tiny potted plant (~1.1 metres away, between the tape machine and paper backdrop) that blends into the cluttered desk in RGB, the segmentation is highly unreliable and inconsistent across frames. In frame 1 it merges the seated person and the camera wearer's hands into a single 'person' instance, in frame 2 it misses the seated person completely, and in frame 5 it drops the seated person again while only segmenting the wearer's right arm. Furthermore, it fails to segment almost all workspace equipment—including the smartphone being manipulated, the tripod-mounted screen with white paper within both people's reach, the reel-to-reel player, and the guitar on the far left.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely blank in frames 1 through 3 and only detects a partial yellow body skeleton for the seated person in the lower-left region of frames 4 and 5, with no magenta hand skeletons detected in any frame. In frames 4 and 5, the detected head, shoulder, and torso keypoints locate the seated person about 0.7 to 0.9 metres below and to the left of the camera wearer, confirming that the person's head and torso are angled forward and slightly right toward the mounted screen and computer monitor rather than looking back at the wearer. In frame 5, an extended right-arm segment on the yellow skeleton indicates the seated person reaching forward toward the tripod base (~0.3 to 0.4 metres in front of their torso), a subtle posture detail that is heavily shadowed and occluded by the paper-taped screen in the RGB strip. However, this map is largely unreliable for broader spatial understanding because steep top-down foreshortening and self-occlusion cause complete detection failures for the seated person in the first three frames and for their lower body throughout. It also completely fails to detect the camera wearer's own arms and hands in the immediate foreground (0.2 to 0.8 metres), providing no information about the wearer's reach or hand-object manipulation of the phone tripod.
